pages.text: "I'll stack higher than the water!" Yuki set a stone by the stream and another on top. It rolled off. "Why does it keep falling?"
"Today, I'll make a three-stone tower!" Water babbled over Yuki's feet. Brown dog Momo splashed front paws at the edge.
Two tries, three tries—crash again! Just a touch made the tower collapse. Grandma looked up from washing greens nearby.
Angry, Yuki threw a stone into the water. "I quit! I can't stack!" Yuki rubbed their eyes with a wet hand.
Grandma chose a flat stone and set it before Yuki. "A wide bottom stone gives the others a place to sit." Yuki stared at it.
Yuki laid the flat stone first, then another. Two stood, then crashed again. "...Still, one more stood than before."
"If It Falls, Stack Again!" Holding their breath, Yuki placed the third stone gently and let go. The tower stood quietly amid the water's babble.
"It stood! A real three-stone tower!" Its reflection wavered in the stream. Momo slapped their tail, scattering drops.
Yuki fixed the scarf knot and chose a fourth stone. "One, a flat stone first! Two, let go gently! Three, stack again if it falls!"
Grandma enclosed Yuki's wet hands in hers. Stacking again after a fall made the tower grow little by little. "If It Falls, Stack Again! Tomorrow, four stones!"
